opportunity: Map of which transglutaminases build the hair follicle: TG2 in the hair germ / early IRS, TG1 and TG5 in outer/inner root sheath cornified envelope, TG3 in the cortex, cuticle and IRS.
tg_fit: Multiple endogenous TGs (TG1/2/3/5) act coordinately; each forms the same epsilon-(gamma-glutamyl)lysine isopeptide bond that mTG also makes. mTG shares the chemistry but is an extracellular microbial enzyme, so it cannot substitute for these intracellular, spatially-programmed follicle enzymes in vivo.
evidence: Reviews and expression studies localize TG2 to the hair germ/IRS of terminal anagen follicles, TG1 and TG5 to ORS/IRS cornified envelope, and TG3 to cortex/cuticle, acting in a highly coordinated manner.

sources.title: Transglutaminase Regulation of Cell Function (Physiol Rev 2014)
Transglutaminase 5 expression in human hair follicle (PubMed 16117804)

verification.note: Isoform localization consistent across a major review and primary expression studies.

opportunity: TG3 crosslinks trichohyalin (TCHH) and keratin intermediate filaments to harden the inner root sheath, giving a rigid scaffold that shapes the growing hair fiber.
tg_fit: This is a TG3-specific, intracellular structural role using epsilon-(gamma-glutamyl)lysine isopeptide bonds. mTG makes the same bond type but on accessible surface Gln/Lys; it cannot reach or replicate the programmed IRS scaffolding inside a living follicle.
evidence: Classic guinea-pig follicle work and modern studies show TG3 catalyzes crosslinking of trichohyalin to keratin filaments, creating the rigid insoluble matrix that reinforces the IRS and supports hair fiber morphogenesis.

Transglutaminase-3 Enzyme: A Putative Actor in Human Hair Shaft Scaffolding? (J Invest Dermatol)

verification.note: TCHH-keratin crosslinking by TG3 is well established structural biology.

opportunity: TG1 (keratinocyte TG) builds the cornified cell envelope in the outer/inner root sheath, sebaceous and sweat glands of anagen hair follicles.
tg_fit: TG1 is membrane-anchored and intracellular. It shares isopeptide chemistry with mTG but its role is barrier/envelope formation, not a target mTG can plausibly reproduce topically.
evidence: Immunolocalization studies detect TG1 in human anagen hair follicles, sebaceous and sweat glands, associated with involucrin in the corneous ORS.

Transglutaminase Regulation of Cell Function (Physiol Rev 2014)

verification.note: Two independent sources confirm TG1 follicular expression.

opportunity: TG2 is the first active transglutaminase detected in the hair germ and in the IRS of terminal anagen follicles, implicated in early terminal differentiation.
tg_fit: TG2 is a multifunctional intracellular/signaling enzyme; its follicular role is differentiation-related, not simply crosslinking hair fiber. mTG (pure crosslinker) cannot reproduce TG2 signaling functions.
evidence: Reviews describe TG2 as present in the bulb/hair germ region and IRS during terminal differentiation, contributing to physical resistance and preservation of the structure.

sources.title: Transglutaminase Regulation of Cell Function (Physiol Rev 2014)

verification.note: Single review source; TG2 follicular role less characterized than TG1/TG3.

opportunity: TG5 is expressed in the human hair follicle (ORS/IRS) and cooperates with TG1 and TG3 to build the cornified cell envelope of the hair-forming compartment.
tg_fit: TG5 is another endogenous intracellular isopeptide crosslinker; shares chemistry with mTG but not accessibility. Confirms redundancy of the isopeptide-crosslinking system in the follicle.
evidence: A dedicated study reports TG5 expression in human hair follicle, detected with involucrin in ORS/IRS; reviews describe TG1/3/5 building the cornified envelope cooperatively.

sources.title: Transglutaminase 5 expression in human hair follicle (PubMed 16117804)
Transglutaminase 3: involvement in epithelial differentiation (Cells 2020)

verification.note: Primary study plus review corroborate TG5 follicular expression.

opportunity: Uncombable hair syndrome (UHS) is caused by recessive mutations in TGM3, PADI3 or TCHH; loss of TG3 function yields misshapen (triangular/grooved) hair shafts.
tg_fit: Direct genetic proof that TG3 crosslinking is needed for correct hair SHAFT SHAPE and combability. Critically, affected individuals still GROW hair in normal quantity - the defect is structural, not growth/quantity.
evidence: Mutations in PADI3/TGM3/TCHH impair post-translational crosslinking of trichohyalin, giving irregular shaft cross-section; hair quantity is unchanged and the phenotype improves with age.

sources.title: Mutations in Three Genes Cause Uncombable Hair Syndrome (Am J Hum Genet 2016)
Uncombable hair syndrome (Wikipedia summary of genetics)
PADI3, hair disorders and genomic investigation (Br J Dermatol 2019)

verification.note: Human genetics ties TG3 to hair STRUCTURE not growth; explicitly hair quantity unchanged.

opportunity: Tgm3-deficient mice (classic wellhaarig 'we' mutants and Tgm3 knockouts) develop wavy coats, curly whiskers, cuticle/torsion defects and shorter keratins - but still grow a hair coat.
tg_fit: Animal loss-of-function confirms TG3 is required for PROPER hair development (shape/mechanics), not for the presence or growth of hair. Removing TG activity does not stop hair growth; it distorts the fiber.
evidence: Four independent wellhaarig alleles map to Tgm3 defects; EM of Tgm3-/- hairs shows irregular torsions, deformed grooves, abnormal cuticle and shorter keratins, with hair still present.

sources.title: The mouse wellhaarig (we) mutations result from defects in Tgm3 (PMC4640993)
Epidermal Transglutaminase (TGase 3) Is Required for Proper Hair Development... (PLOS One 2012)

verification.note: Two independent mouse studies: TG3 loss = structural hair defect, not loss of growth.

opportunity: Testing the core hypothesis 'TG has a hair-growth effect, so mTG could too.'
tg_fit: VERDICT: The hair-growth framing is not supported. TG's documented role is building/shaping the hair fiber (structural), and high TG activity in growing (anagen) follicles is a CONSEQUENCE of active fiber synthesis, not a driver of proliferation. No peer-reviewed study shows any TG - and specifically not mTG - increasing hair growth rate, density, or reversing hairloss.
evidence: Genetic loss of TG3 leaves hair quantity unchanged (UHS); TG activity correlates with anagen because it crosslinks the forming fiber; the therapeutic patent direction is to INHIBIT TG to REDUCE unwanted hair, the opposite of a growth promoter.

sources.title: Uncombable hair syndrome - hair quantity unchanged
Alteration of rate and character of hair growth - TG inhibitor patent (WO1992011007A1)

verification.note: No evidence TG/mTG promotes hair growth; the 'growth' claim is a misreading of TG's structural/anagen-associated role.

opportunity: Microbial TG (Streptomyces mobaraensis) applied topically to damaged hair increased tensile strength by ~15.6% and improved surface luster and reduced friction.
tg_fit: This is the strongest real mTG-on-hair evidence and it is about STRENGTHENING/REPAIR of existing fiber via surface isopeptide crosslinking, NOT growth. Directly plausible for mTG because it acts on accessible keratin Gln/Lys residues ex vivo.
evidence: 'Application of Transglutaminase for Hair Revitalization' (J. Soc. Cosmet. Sci. Korea) reports mTG raised hair tensile strength 15.64% vs control and improved surface properties on damaged hair.

sources.title: Application of Transglutaminase for Hair Revitalization (J Soc Cosmet Sci Korea)

verification.note: Single peer-reviewed cosmetic-science study; effect is strengthening, explicitly not growth.

opportunity: mTG combined with hydrolysed keratin/serine repairs damaged hair fiber: fracture stress rose from 1.03 to 1.81 N, fracture strain 9.5 to 19.9 mm, alkali solubility dropped ~50%.
tg_fit: mTG grafts keratin/amino donors onto damaged fiber via epsilon-(gamma-glutamyl)lysine bonds, restoring mechanical integrity. Highly plausible mTG use-case; again a REPAIR/strengthening benefit, not growth.
evidence: Peer-reviewed Polymers (2023) study: TGase-crosslinked keratin repair solution significantly improved fracture stress/strain and reduced alkali solubility of damaged hair.

opportunity: Korean patents claim damaged-hair restoration compositions containing transglutaminase (with amino-acid binding agents/peptides or chestnut extract) to crosslink and repair hair.
tg_fit: Commercial IP already positions mTG as a hair-REPAIR/fixation active that crosslinks keratin. Confirms industry sees mTG as a bond-builder, not a growth agent.
evidence: KR101017461B1 and KR101510308B1 disclose transglutaminase-containing compositions for restoring damaged hair via protein crosslinking.

verification.note: Two patents corroborate mTG as a hair-repair crosslinker.

opportunity: mTG isopeptide (Gln-Lys) crosslinking as an alternative/complement to disulfide 'bond builders' like Olaplex, which reconnect broken cystine bonds.
tg_fit: Conceptually, mTG could act as an 'isopeptide bond builder': it forms covalent amide crosslinks between glutamine and lysine, a different bond chemistry than Olaplex's thiol/disulfide targeting. Plausible as a complementary repair mechanism; unproven as a marketed bond-builder and no growth claim.
evidence: Olaplex-class agents rebuild disulfide bridges; mTG forms independent epsilon-(gamma-glutamyl)lysine crosslinks, and wool/hair fibers treated with TGase show smoother scales and improved strength.

Enzymatic Crosslinking of Amino Acids Improves Keratin Repair on Hair (Polymers 2023)

verification.note: Chemistry supports an isopeptide bond-builder concept; not a demonstrated commercial Olaplex analogue.

opportunity: The patented therapeutic use of transglutaminase in hair is an INHIBITOR to REDUCE androgen-stimulated (unwanted) hair growth / hirsutism - the direct opposite of a growth promoter.
tg_fit: Because TG activity is required to build the hair fiber, blocking it thins/alters hair. This strongly argues that adding mTG would not stimulate growth; if anything the growth axis is served by inhibition, not addition.
evidence: Patents claim topical transglutaminase inhibitors to alter the rate and character of androgen-stimulated hair growth, with later hirsutism-treatment patents noting TG inhibitors can be added to reduce unwanted hair.

Topical hirsutism treatment (US20180250212A1)

verification.note: Patent-level evidence; direction of intervention (inhibition) contradicts a growth-promotion hypothesis.

opportunity: Overall plausibility of mTG delivering a hair benefit: separate 'can crosslink hair keratin' from 'promotes hair growth.'
tg_fit: PLAUSIBLE: mTG can covalently crosslink accessible hair-shaft keratin (surface Gln/Lys), strengthening and repairing fibers ex vivo/topically. NOT PLAUSIBLE: mTG promoting biological hair growth - a ~38 kDa microbial enzyme cannot penetrate to the follicle bulb/matrix, and growth is driven by stem-cell/Wnt signaling, not extracellular isopeptide crosslinking.
evidence: Multiple studies show mTG strengthens/repairs damaged hair fiber via isopeptide bonds, while endogenous follicle TGs act intracellularly on differentiation; no data link extracellular mTG to hair-growth signaling.
